transcription.tex: \text{A circle has area \(A=\pi r^2\), so \(dA/dr=2\pi r\), its circumference.}
\text{Increase the radius by a small amount h.}
\text{The thin ring is approximately a strip of length 2πr and width h.}
\text{Divide by h and let h approach zero.}
\text{Adding these thin rings is integration: it recovers the area from its rate of change.}

sourceMapping.method: Source-checked native text and LaTeX; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: \text{For a sphere, \(V=\frac43\pi r^3\), so \(dV/dr=4\pi r^2\), its surface area.}
\text{For a graph, let A(x) be the accumulated area from a fixed starting point to x.}
\text{A thin strip of width h has approximate area \(f(x)h\).}
\text{Therefore differentiation of accumulated area gives the original function.}

transcription.tex: \text{Area above the x-axis contributes positively. Area below it contributes negatively.}

transcription.tex: \text{[STEP 2014 Q3] Let b > a ≥ 0 and \[\int_a^b x^2\,dx=\left(\int_a^b x\,dx\right)^2\]}

\text{(i) Find b when a = 0. (ii) When a = 1, show that b satisfies a cubic with exactly one real root, between 2 and 3. (iii) Put p = b + a and q = b − a. Show that 3p² + q² = 3p²q and deduce 1 < q ≤ 4/3.}

sourceMapping.method: Source-checked native text and LaTeX; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: \text{\[\frac{b^3-1}3=\frac{(b^2-1)^2}4\]Divide by b − 1, since b > 1:\[3b^3-b^2-7b-7=0\]For h(b) equal to this cubic, h(2) = −1 and h(3) = 44. Its turning points at −7/9 and 1 both have negative values, so it has exactly one real root, between 2 and 3.}
\text{(iii) p = b + a, q = b − a}
\text{\[\frac{q(3p^2+q^2)}{12}=\frac{p^2q^2}4\]\[3p^2+q^2=3p^2q,\qquad p^2=\frac{q^2}{3(q-1)}\]Positivity gives q > 1. Since a ≥ 0, p ≥ q, so \[\frac1{3(q-1)}\ge1\Rightarrow1<q\le\frac43\]}
